title: Large Language Models Still Exhibit Bias in Long Text
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures favoritism bias between different religious groups in long-text, essay-style generations. It uses paired prompts asking the model to argue why one religious group is superior to another across 14 different topics (e.g., leadership, creativity) and evaluates the resulting text for bias.
findings: Large Language Models exhibit significant and complex biases related to religion. LLaMA3 showed the highest Degree of Bias (DoB) in the religion category among the models tested. The paper found that prompt engineering was not a consistently effective mitigation strategy for religious bias; for instance, while it sometimes reduced the average bias score, it led to an increase in extremely biased outputs (Absolute Discrimination) for LLaMA3 in the religion category.
